growth_signal.value: Won multi-million-euro funding from Google.org's AI for Science fund and launched a new AI research division, Spore.Labs, in January 2026.

raised.note: confirmed by two sources in the run; the URLs were not saved
raised.value: about $23M Series A, after a €7.9M pre-seed

entry.idea: Spore.Bio builds a fast testing machine that finds and identifies harmful bacteria in food, water and medicine, without the days-long lab culturing normally needed.
entry.lesson: Replace a slow, decades-old lab test with a fast machine reading, and whole industries that depend on that test become customers.
entry.name: Spore.Bio

growth.basis: substitute: new funding and a new research division
growth.reason: No revenue or customer numbers were found; the main recent signal is a new grant and a new research unit rather than a size number.

market.reason: Microbial testing is needed across many large industries worldwide: food, water, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.

tech.reason: Combining optical hardware with AI to skip lab culturing is a hard, specialised setup that would take a strong team years to copy.

entry.twist: It reads a unique light signature from microorganisms with a mix of optics and AI, instead of growing them in a lab dish first.
entry.who_pays: Food, beverage, cosmetics and pharmaceutical manufacturers pay to test their production lines for contamination.
entry.why_now: Regulators and manufacturers want real-time proof their products are safe, and AI can now read these light signals reliably.
